    fix: don't let findInaccessiblePlugin re-find a binary via a relative PATH entry
    
    exec.LookPath deliberately refuses (exec.ErrDot) to resolve a binary
    found via a relative $PATH entry -- Go's fix for the classic "dot in
    PATH" RCE class. resolvePlugin's fallback for LookPath failures,
    findInaccessiblePlugin, didn't distinguish that refusal from a genuine
    "exists but lacks the executable bit" case: it re-walked the same PATH
    entries with a plain os.Stat and returned found=true for the exact
    file LookPath just refused. runPlugin then exec'd it via a path
    containing a separator, which bypasses Go's exec.Command ErrDot
    re-check (that only fires for a bare name with no separator).
    
    Net effect: any relative $PATH entry (direnv PATH_add, a project-local
    bin/, node_modules/.bin-style patterns -- all common, not exotic) plus
    an untrusted repo containing <relative-dir>/entire-<name> gave silent
    code execution with the user's full privileges on `entire <name>`.
    
    Fix: findInaccessiblePlugin now only scans absolute PATH entries,
    mirroring exec.LookPath's own refusal for the relative case.

    shebang'd binary planted under a relative bin/ directory, PATH set to
    include it, MaybeRunPlugin invoked directly, and a marker file assert
    proving the binary was never executed. Confirmed the test would have

My commit fixed it by factoring the rule into `execx.PathScanDirs()`, shared with the external-agent scanner. I kept the refactored version and folded upstream's call-site-specific rationale into the comment: the detail that this function runs *only after* `LookPath` failed, so re-walking relative entries would re-find the exact binary `LookPath` refused with `ErrDot`, which `runPlugin` then execs via a separator-bearing path that bypasses `exec.Command`'s re-check. - `updateSummaryGenerationSettings` was the only one of four grant sites ordering the write *before* the struct save; the other three already do it after and document why. Two tests reproduced it (`--local`, and a local-only repo): the notice printed while the grant was silently dropped. The existing test missed it because it only exercises the project-file target, where the two writes touch different files.

input.command:
git add CLAUDE.md cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider_test.go cmd/entire/cli/setup.go cmd/entire/cli/setup_external_agents.go cmd/entire/cli/setup_external_agents_test.go && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
narrow the external_agents grant and stop announcing inert ones

Four review findings on the executable-resolution work.

discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing had the provider name in hand and still
called DiscoverAndRegisterAlways, which globs every absolute $PATH entry
and runs every entire-agent-* binary's info subcommand. The name comes
from summary_generation.provider, honored from the COMMITTED
.entire/settings.json, so one settings line in a pull request reached the
full sweep on whoever pulled it. Route it through the named lookup that
already existed for the --summarize-provider override, renamed from
discoverDispatchSummaryProvider to discoverNamedSummaryProvider now that
two paths share it.

The non-interactive branches of resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider select a
provider with no human involved (the only candidate, or the first of
several on a headless run) and persisted the external_agents grant on the
way through. That grant is repo-wide rather than scoped to the chosen
provider. Gate it on summarySelectionOrigin so only a pick at the prompt
flips it. The provider name is still persisted: it grants nothing by
itself, and an auto-selected external provider keeps resolving through
the named ungated lookup above, so nothing is lost at runtime.

enableExternalAgentsLocally reported success for a write that cannot take
effect. A tracked settings.local.json makes loadMergedSettings drop the
whole local layer, and the usual rejection channel stays silent because
enforceExternalAgentsTrust returns early on !s.ExternalAgents, which is
the state a dropped layer produces. So the user saw "external agents are
now enabled" over a grant nothing would ever read. Read the grant back
and return whether it verified, preferring whichever rejection channel
recorded something. Not an error: one committed file must not fail the
command. persistSummaryProviderSelection is a fifth route to the same
false claim and gets the same read-back.

CLAUDE.md's new absolute-paths section read as a blanket rule while
redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command is exec'd with no cmd.Dir and no
absoluteness check. Name it as the deliberate exception, with the reason
the trust gate makes it one.

EOF
